title: Polarization-dependent exchange effects in intrabeam scattering
summary: The emittance growth due to intrabeam scattering (IBS) depends on the scattering cross section and is therefore affected by the exchange interaction of identical particles. However, as the IBS growth rates are typically dominated by small-angle scattering events and the exchange interaction only significantly alters the cross section at relatively large angles, the influence of the exchange interaction is usually small. In this paper, we calculate the small corrections to the growth rates resulting from the exchange interaction. We include the polarization dependence of the exchange term in the cross section, and so we also present the growth rates as a function of the beam polarization.

title: Scaling laws for contamination traversal times during vacuum breaks in superconducting accelerators
summary: A sudden loss of vacuum in a superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) accelerator drives warm gas into the evacuated beamline, where it propagates through interconnected SRF cavities cooled by liquid helium, causing surface contamination, intense heat deposition, and dangerous pressure buildup. Yet predicting how such a failure propagates through realistic multicell cavities has remained difficult because compressible gas dynamics, condensation and cryogenic heat transfer are strongly coupled. Here we develop and experimentally validate a multidimensional computational framework that resolves these processes, and apply it to a full-scale nine-cell SRF cavity. We find that the repeated cell geometry produces staircase-like gas-front propagation, as impingement, recirculation and localized cryopumping strongly retard the bulk flow within each cell. Across a broad range of breach sizes, the cavity traversal time follows a robust power-law scaling with leakage area, providing quantitative guidance for the response time of beamline isolation and protection systems. The simulations also reveal a geometry-confined Mach disk whose position and size track the advancing gas front, suggesting that its acoustic emission could potentially enable rapid, non-invasive detection and localization of vacuum failures. These findings pave the way for a new generation of predictive diagnostics and protection strategies to safeguard large-scale superconducting accelerators.

title: Construction of crystal-based light sources with LWFA electron beams
summary: We discuss a possibility to construct a crystal-based light source (CLS) of gamma-rays using electron beams produce by Laser Wake Field Acceleration (LWFA). This state-of-the-art acceleration technique is capable of producing few-GeV, ultra-short (fs) electron beams. In the case studies presented, we demonstrate the feasibility of novel gamma-ray CLSs based on exposing single crystals to electron beams available at the ELI-ELBA. The results of rigorous numerical simulations are presented to characterise the radiation emitted emitted by 1 and 4 GeV electrons incident on a 200-micron-thick single silicon crystal along the (110) plane. The simulations were performed using the current divergence as well as a smaller value that is believed to be a realistic to achieve in the near future. We demonstrate that it is feasible to achieve a photon yield of $10^6-10^7$ photons/s in the photon energy range from 5 to 50 MeV. Looking further ahead, we also performed a similar analysis for a 4-GeV positron beam incident on much thicker targets, up to 2 mm oriented silicon crystal. In this case, the photon yield can be increased by an order of magnitude.

title: A General Treatment of Coupled Cavity Resonators
summary: Consider several cavity resonators whose resonant frequencies and electromagnetic fields are known, and suppose that they are coupled through apertures. How can the resonant frequencies and resonant electromagnetic fields of the resulting coupled-cavity resonator be expressed in terms of the original resonant frequencies and electromagnetic fields? This is a problem frequently encountered in radio-frequency systems for accelerators. One example is a multicell cavity used in high-energy electron accelerators. In this note, the resonant frequencies and resonant electromagnetic fields of such coupled cavities are examined as generally as possible, based only on Maxwell's equations and boundary conditions. Specifically, the response function of a cavity as viewed from its coupling ports, namely, its admittance matrix, is derived, and a formulation is developed to express the coupled resonant electromagnetic fields using this matrix. The resulting formulation shows that the coupled resonant modes can be described in terms of overlap integrals between the resonant modes of the cavities and the waveguide modes at the coupling apertures. It also shows that the coupled resonant frequencies are given by the zeros of the determinant of a matrix constructed from the admittance matrices. The results thus obtained are applied to simple systems to confirm the validity of the formulation. Numerical calculations based on this formulation are also carried out for periodic systems in an attempt to derive dispersion relations.

title: Micrometer-thin liquid sheets from single-jet impact on a sharp edge for multi-kHz laser-plasma experiments
summary: We present a simple and robust method for generating freely suspended liquid sheets by directing a single laminar liquid jet onto the sharp edge of an inclined plate. By optimizing liquid composition, impact geometry, and flow conditions, we identify a 60:40 ethylene-glycol-deionized-water volumetric mixture for stable sheet formation. The resulting sheets span 8 mm in height and 3 mm in width, with thicknesses from 1.1 to 4.8 micrometers measured by spatial and spectral interferometry. Operated in vacuum as continuously renewed plasma mirrors, these targets demonstrate stable performance from 0.5 to 10 kHz using 175-fs Yb:KGW laser pulses, reaching a maximum S-polarized reflectivity of 66.5% at an intensity of 4 x 10^14 W/cm^2. At higher intensities using 25-fs Ti:sapphire pulses at 1 kHz, maximum S-polarized reflectivity reaches 77% at 2 x 10^16 W/cm^2. The reflected beam exhibits high temporal stability, with angular pointing fluctuations of 18.19 +/- 0.53 microradians. Our results demonstrate a tunable, continuously renewed liquid-sheet target for multi-kHz laser-plasma experiments.

title: Modeling and control of traveling wave structures with arbitrary beam loading
summary: Traveling wave (TW) structures are widely used in linear or circular accelerators for beam acceleration. Unlike the standing wave cavities, the overall accelerating voltage cannot be measured by the probes installed in the TW structures. This creates difficulties measuring and regulating the accelerating voltage and phase felt by the beam when it passes through the structure. In this paper, a model of TW structures is developed, allowing us to estimate the accelerating voltage and phase from the measurement of the RF drive power input to the TW structure. The beam loading effects, i.e., the beam-induced accelerating voltage and phase in the TW structure, are also included in the model. With the TW structure model, control methods are proposed to stabilize the accelerating voltage and phase felt by the beam based on feedback, feedforward, and optimization. The validity of the TW structure model is confirmed with the test results at the SwissFEL with improved beam stability under the same RF feedback controller. This work provides a firm basis for developing the multiple-bunch operation strategy for SwissFEL required by the future upgrade with more beamlines.

title: Reconstruction of Unobserved Core Electron Density in Tokamak Plasmas with a Neural Operator Transport Surrogate and Uncertainty Quantification
summary: Real-time control of tokamak plasmas requires the electron density profile. However, in a reactor-relevant device, diagnostic port access is limited and the profile can be observed only partially. In the present work we reconstruct the density profile by inferring the coefficients of a physics-based one-dimensional particle transport equation, using a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) surrogate of the transport solver as a fast differentiable forward model. The surrogate enables realtime-compatible gradient-based reconstruction and uncertainty quantification from the reflectometry and interferometry measurements. We compare four uncertainty quantification methods - multi-seed ensembles, the Laplace approximation, Metropolis-Hastings, and a Gaussian method independent of the reconstruction fit. The resulting uncertainty is scored with CRPS and coverage calibration, separately on the observed and unobserved regions. We further demonstrate advantage of our approach over standard analytical function fit on synthetic and experimental DIII-D discharges.

title: One Component Plasmas Frequency Moments from the ISF
summary: Dynamic structural characteristics of classical one component plasmas (OCP) are an essential tool for understanding of strongly coupled plasmas through experiments and numerical simulations. Here, instead of the dynamic structure factor, we focus our attention on the intermediate scattering function (ISF). Theoretical results are compared to those of obtained by the method of molecular dynamics (MD).

title: Reduced Molecular Plasma Kinetics with Non-Boltzmann Vibrational Distribution
summary: Vibrational kinetics can strongly affect energy transfer, chemical kinetics, and discharge behavior in molecular plasmas, but resolving all internal states is often impractical for reactor-scale simulation. Compact, physics-based vibrational closures are particularly needed when complete state-to-state (StS) data are limited. Starting from a detailed $\mathrm{H}_2$ StS plasma-kinetics framework coupled to an electron-Boltzmann calculation, this work develops a reduced vibrational-kinetics formulation. The $\mathrm{H}_2$ vibrational ladder is reduced to two non-Boltzmann groups that evolve their population and internal energy. State-resolved reaction rates and associated energy-exchange terms are projected onto the groups for subsequent tabulation in reactor-scale plasma models. StS-informed samples of the reduced-model are propagated for pulsed RF $\mathrm{H}_2$ plasmas across a scan of pulse-averaged absorbed power and compared with the corresponding StS simulations. Predictions from the sampled models reproduce the bulk plasma response, including electron density, atomic-H density, and $\mathrm{H}_3^+$ density. Discrepancies in $\mathrm{H}^-$ production and the upper-energy-group vibrational temperature persist across the sampled reductions. This indicates a limitation of the present VDF reconstruction rather than the nominal parameter choice. Tail-sensitive processes therefore require a more accurate representation of the vibrational distribution.

title: Experimental verification of the PRIORA Monte Carlo code for proton radiography
summary: PRIORA (Proton Radiography Ion-Optical Ray-tracing Analysis) is a fast Monte Carlo model for high-energy proton radiography. It combines fitted proton-matter interaction tables with energy-dependent transfer maps of arbitrary order and simulates approximately $10^6$ protons/s through a complete ion-optical system on an 8-core laptop. We verify it with GSI data obtained with the Ta_bench target: fifteen precision slits in a 2 mm Ta plate between symmetric PMMA staircases. A single experimental image provides the image scale, spatial resolution as a function of chromatic load, signed focus in both planes, effective angular acceptance and multiple-scattering contrast. With identical processing of experiment and simulation and no physics adjustment, PRIORA reproduces the data obtained with 2 and 4 GeV protons. At 2 GeV, PRIORA also recovers sub-percent quadrupole trims consistent with the control-system records and determines a target-plane spatial resolution of $115\pm6\,μ$m.

title: Reinforcement Learning Controllers for Fusion Scenario Development
summary: Scenario development, the design of the waveforms that take a tokamak discharge from breakdown to flat-top, is still an iterative, labour-intensive process. Every candidate scenario has to be simulated with a controller in the loop, and the classical shape and current controllers need low-level actuator references. So the process is iterative and includes a number of trial-and-error steps. We propose to replace the per-scenario controller tuning by a single goal-conditioned reinforcement-learning controller trained once, in advance, against a free-boundary equilibrium and transport simulator. A scenario is then specified only by the target waveforms of the physical quantities of interest (plasma current, line-averaged electron density, LCFS shape, x-point positions), and the controller produces the coil-current and fueling commands that realize them. We demonstrate the approach on an EAST plasma-current ramp-up: the controller takes over a small limited plasma, ramps the current and the density, grows the cross-section, forms two x-points and holds a double-null diverted configuration against sampled shape targets for the rest of a 1.2 s episode. The neural network controller is trained using TQC algorithm. On 1024 test scenarios sampled from a low-discrepancy scrambled Sobol sequence in 11-dimensional target space, the controller forms the divertor in 86% of the cases, holds it for more than 0.5 s in 67% and reaches the end of the episode in a diverted state in 58%, with flat-top tracking errors of a few kA in plasma current, $\sim 0.15\times10^{19}$ m$^{-3}$ in density, $\sim 2$ cm in position and $\sim 8$ cm in x-point location; the failures concentrate at the high-current density ($J$) region which is believed to be physically or from engineering perspective not feasible within ohmic mode.

title: Beyond Radiation Hydrodynamics: A Coupled Kinetic Plasma and Radiation Modeling of NIF Polar Direct Drive Capsule
summary: Predictive modeling of inertial-confinement-fusion (ICF) implosions increasingly requires resolving ion-kinetic effects beyond the reach of radiation-hydrodynamics, without sacrificing radiation transport. We present, to our knowledge, the first coupling of a kinetic-ion plasma model to thermal radiation transport. The iFP code - a conservative, spherically symmetric, 1D2V hybrid kinetic-ion/fluid-electron Vlasov-Fokker-Planck solver - is extended with a grey P1 radiation model, coupled through a high-order/low-order (HOLO) fixed-point solver and advanced on a shared adaptive moving mesh. Opacities are mixed on the fly from the LANL TOPS library, exploiting the per-species information intrinsic to a kinetic code. We verify the implementation against the optically thick Marshak-wave and Mach-45 radiative-shock benchmarks, and apply it to a NIF polar-direct-drive exploding-pusher capsule. Increasing physics fidelity systematically improves agreement with the measured neutron yield and burn width; the improvement is driven by kinetically enhanced fuel leakage and ballistic preheating, and radiation transport proves essential for quantitative agreement. This work establishes a proof-of-principle capability for higher-fidelity kinetic-plasma/radiation modeling of ICF.

title: Ion Heating in Pair-loaded Relativistic Turbulence
summary: Pair-loaded relativistic turbulence is expected in compact high-energy astrophysical environments and may sustain plasma heating. Using self-consistent three-dimensional radiative particle-in-cell simulations, we identify the mechanism of ion heating mediated by pair-enhanced radiative feedback in relativistic turbulence. We derive the theoretical criterion for the transition to a regime dominated by radiative feedback and show that pair loading promotes the growth and persistence of large, connected optically thick structures. These long-lived structures sustain intense localized ion heating, repeatedly generating prominent hot-ion clumps and substantially enhancing the mean ion temperature. Our results establish a physical link between pair creation and sustained ion heating, providing a theoretical basis for investigating intermittent hot-ion production in black-hole coronae and gamma-ray burst outflows.
